accepted.question_text: Let M be a compact connected Sasaki manifold with fixed underlying contact CR structure (D, J). Its Sasaki cone kappa(D, J) is the moduli space of Sasaki metrics with that fixed CR structure, and in the unreduced cone t^+(D, J) these structures come in rays under transverse scaling. Must every ray represented by a Sasaki metric of constant scalar curvature be isolated among the rays in the Sasaki cone?
accepted.context_brief: Isolation of cscS rays in the Sasaki cone

evidence.quote: The purpose of this paper is to discuss two open problems in Sasaki geometry. These problems involve the so-called Sasaki cone ... This leads to two important open problems: Problem 1. Are constant scalar curvature rays in the Sasaki cone isolated?

The Sasaki cone kappa(D, J) can be thought of as the moduli space of Sasaki metrics with a fixed underlying contact CR structure (D, J) where D is the contact bundle and J is a complex structure on D.
So Sasakian structures in t^+ (D, J) come in rays.

accepted.question_text: Let M be a compact connected Sasaki manifold with fixed underlying contact CR structure (D, J), and let its Sasaki cone be the cone of rays of Sasaki metrics compatible with that structure. Suppose the cone contains an extremal ray, meaning a ray represented by a Sasaki metric whose scalar curvature has transversely holomorphic gradient; constant scalar curvature Sasaki metrics are a special case of extremal metrics. Does it follow that the same Sasaki cone must contain at least one constant scalar curvature ray?
accepted.context_brief: From extremal rays to existence of a cscS ray

evidence.quote: Problem 2. If there are extremal rays of Sasaki metrics in the Sasaki cone, is there always at least one constant scalar curvature ray?
We are also interested in the moduli space e(D, J) of extremal Sasaki metrics as well as the moduli space kappa_csc (D, J) of constant scalar curvature Sasaki metrics.
Such Sasaki metrics (structures) are called extremal. An important special case are the Sasaki metrics of constant scalar curvature (cscS) ... So extremal and cscS Sasakian structures come in rays.
